successors.name: British Colonial Empire
successors.text: Bunyoro of the mid-nineteenth century, 'a far smaller state': the Bunyoro region with Kibaale (Buyaga and Bugangaizi, the 'lost counties' of 1964)

ledger.x: Late 16th century: Rukidi-Mpuga founds the Bunyoro kingdom.
End of the 18th century: Buganda seizes Kooki and Buddu.
1899: Kabalega is captured and Bunyoro annexed.

wars.name: Battle of Rwangabi
wars.outcome: Bunyoro victory in February 1886: its army 'achieved a significant victory against the Baganda', outnumbered, in the struggle over the ivory trade; no border moved.

wars.name: Bunyoro resistance to the British
wars.outcome: British victory: 'Kabalega... resisted the efforts of Great Britain' to take control; he was captured in 1899 and exiled to the Seychelles and Bunyoro was annexed.

certainty.note: Kingdom frontiers are approximate; the pages give an area and the names of provinces, no line.
